newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday with a large number of new domestic shares debuting on the stock markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 15.00 percent from 13.20 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 2.4 million lots from 3.1 million lots. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Six new domestic A share firms debuted on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges on Friday, boosting money demand on the repo market and pushing up the rates, traders said.
In addition, Guangzhou Power Enterprise (Holdings) Co Ltd issued 100 million A shares on the Shanghai bourse.
"The heavy issue helped boost short-term fund demand, in particular supporting the seven-day contract," said one trader.
But the weak performance of the A share markets will prevent the rates from rising further, traders said.
Traders said they expect the contracts to undergo a technical correction on Wednesday next week.
The T-bill market will be closed from Saturday to Tuesday to mark China's takeover of Hong Kong, the exchange has announced.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Friday on a technical rebound after weeks of downside trading, traders said.
The most actively traded 3-year bond that matures in August 1999 rose to 107.86 yuan from 107.70 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell sharply to 471,021 lots from 876,210 lots.
Despite Friday's rise, traders said the spot contracts had not ended their downward trend and could be expected to continue to fall next week.
